senior-living-leaders-ai-adoption-in-sen.author: Kyle Gardner
senior-living-leaders-ai-adoption-in-sen.core: Posted in last 7 days Senior Living Leaders - AI Adoption in Senior Housing Great conversation with Jessie Lucci and Lucas McCurdy Senior Living Fan 📣 on The Signal podcast's first episode! Lucas approached me with an idea he had been marinating on... a podcast where the discussion would focus on technology in our industry. AI conversations are happening everywhere, but there wasn't much focused on our senior housing. I was hesitant at first, because I don't really view myself as an AI expert. I am curious about it, I want to leverage it in my personal life and business, and I have enjoyed learning about it and experimenting with it. I'm approaching this podcast with the goal of learning in public and sharing my experiences. I want to speak with people who are experimenting, testing, and building with AI and learn from them - with you. AI is prominent in the technology of daily living for most of the planet. ChatGPT and Google's Gemini each have 1B+ MAUs and Meta has engrained AI into its products which are used by 1/4 of the planet. NIC MAP ran a survey recently where respondents confirmed that AI is heavily used at work. 86% of respondents use it for work and 79% of them use it daily. This technology is moving fast. Let's learn how to use it together.

executive-search-firms-ai-impact-on-juni.author: Grace Hamza
executive-search-firms-ai-impact-on-juni.core: Posted in last 7 days Executive Search Firms - AI Impact On Junior Learning If AI does the junior work in executive search, how will junior people learn? In Nexco.ai's latest research, 72% of search firms explicitly kept relationships, assessment or final judgement in human hands. Yet many are already using, or planning to use, AI for earlier stages of the work, including mapping and document drafting. It got me thinking about how that judgement developed in my own career. Preparing a candidate report involves noticing where the evidence is thin, deciding what matters and having your conclusions challenged by someone more experienced. As AI takes on more of the preparation, those opportunities to learn may become less obvious, and certainly less automatic. Firms will need to deliberately create opportunities for learning. For example, junior colleagues could spend more time in client conversations and discussing difficult assessments with partners. That would require experienced people to make time, and juniors to have enough involvement to form a view of their own. But it could also offer a much richer and faster learning experience than the way many of us learned. I’d be interested to hear how search firms are thinking about this as part of our research for the third edition of the State of AI in Executive Search report. If you’d like to contribute, or see a copy of the current report, please comment or send me a message. Nexco.ai
